business_problem: Instability in the Silica/Magnesia (S/M) ratio within slag furnaces led to suboptimal slag flow, reduced output, long response delays, and heavy reliance on continuous manual adjustments by engineers and operators.
solution_summary: PT Vale implemented an in-house machine learning automation platform to control the Silica/Magnesia ratio in nickel slag furnaces. The system combines real-time data integration from plant operations with XRF laboratory analysis and a neural-network model to evaluate furnace conditions and determine the conveyor speed adjustments needed to keep the slag ratio within target. The model output is connected directly to field control systems and PLC control systems, allowing autonomous decisions for West Block and East Block conveyors instead of waiting for manual intervention. Process analysis, automation engineering, laboratory testing, and quality assurance were combined into a single operating loop. The source does not identify a separate storage platform, but it clearly describes a closed-loop AI control architecture that ingests operational and lab data, computes control actions, and serves them directly to production equipment in near real time.

data_flow: Operational data from the slag furnace process is integrated in real time and combined with XRF laboratory analysis inputs. A neural-network model evaluates the S/M ratio condition and generates control decisions, which are sent through field control systems and PLC control systems to adjust West Block and East Block conveyor speeds automatically.
business_outcome: PT Vale improved slag-ratio compliance, removed the need for continuous manual adjustment, increased process reliability, reduced operator burden and delays, enabled potential nickel recovery gains, lowered operational risk, and created a foundation to extend smart automation into sulfur and coal management.
